papers.title_en: RECAP: Calibrating Low-Bit Reasoning Models on the History They Read
papers.authors: Chi Ruan, Yujie Chen, Zixiang Zhao, Jingcai Guo, Haotong Qin
papers.evidence: 面向低比特推理模型的后训练量化校准
papers.tldr: 低比特量化虽降低推理模型服务成本，却会沿长思维链累积误差，且标准校准只用短片段、缺失后续步骤依赖的历史上下文。RECAP 提出动态前缀校准，将长历史上下文与短块重建分离，并用前缀读取几何按注意力影响非对称加权键值误差。该方法仅在校准阶段应用，在 W4A4KV4 下于 MATH500 提升13.3个百分点、AIME-120提升15.8个百分点。结果说明低比特推理校准时保留历史依赖至关重要。
papers.abstract_en: Low-bit quantization reduces the cost of serving reasoning models but can substantially degrade long chains of thought. Each step reads cached keys and values spanning thousands of tokens, allowing quantization errors to accumulate along the trajectory. Standard calibration operates on short segments that omit the earlier context needed by later reasoning steps. Even when this context is retained, cache reconstruction error alone does not capture how quantization errors affect subsequent attention. We present RECAP, a post-training quantization method that calibrates reasoning models on the history they read. Dynamic-prefix calibration separates long historical context from short-block reconstruction. It regenerates prefix keys and values with the current quantizer and rotates the active block to supervise every position along the trajectory. Prefix read geometry further supervises historical cache errors according to their effects on attention outputs, weighting key and value errors asymmetrically. With both components applied only during calibration, RECAP outperforms the baseline across multiple reasoning models and quantization settings. Under W4A4KV4, RECAP improves accuracy over the baseline by 13.3 percentage points on MATH500 with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and 15.8 points on AIME-120 with Qwen3-4B. These results highlight the importance of preserving historical dependencies during calibration for low-bit reasoning.

papers.title_en: HGA-Quant: Heterogeneity-Aware Quantization for AutoRegressive Visual Generation Models
papers.authors: Xinmeng Liu, Xianglong Yan, Kaicheng Yang, Weisheng Dong, Yulun Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向低比特视觉生成模型的无训练后训练量化
papers.tldr: 自回归视觉生成模型计算与内存开销大，低比特后训练量化又常导致图像质量明显下降。本文提出免训练PTQ框架HGA-Quant，包含尾部感知有界初始化网格细化T-BGR与由粗到细激活精度调度CAPS。在多个ARVG骨干上，该方法在激进低比特下保持稳健，Infinity上以有效W4A5.6接近全精度生成质量。其贡献在于兼顾权重校准与混合精度分配，提升边缘部署可行性。
papers.abstract_en: Recently, AutoRegressive Visual Generation (ARVG) models have emerged as a competitive paradigm for high-quality image synthesis. However, their substantial computational and memory demands make them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained edge devices. Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) provides a promising solution to reduce the computational and memory costs of ARVG models, yet existing methods often suffer from substantial image quality degradation under low-bit quantization. In this paper, we propose a training-free PTQ framework for ARVG, consisting of Tail-Aware Bounded-init Grid Refinement (T-BGR) and Coarse-to-Fine Activation Precision Scheduling (CAPS). T-BGR introduces a tail-aware reconstruction objective for weight quantizer calibration, assigning greater importance to distribution-tail coefficients and preserving fine-grained information without introducing additional parameters or high-precision branches. CAPS performs coarse-to-fine activation precision scheduling by jointly considering the importance and computational cost of different generation stages, enabling efficient mixed-precision allocation under a given bit budget. Extensive experiments on multiple ARVG backbones demonstrate that our framework consistently improves robustness under aggressive low-bit quantization. Notably, on Infinity, our framework achieves near full-precision image generation quality at an effective W4A5.6 activation precision, while existing methods at W4A6 still exhibit noticeable quality degradation or inconsistent performance. Code is available at https://github.com/lxm-lc/HGA-Quant.

papers.title_en: E8 Lattice Key Quantization for Low-Bit KV-Cache Compression
papers.authors: Sasho Nedelkoski, Alexander Acker, Soeren Becker, Dominik Scheinert, Odej Kao
papers.evidence: 面向LLM的KV缓存低比特向量量化压缩
papers.tldr: 长上下文LLM推理受KV缓存显存限制，低比特标量量化在2-bit键上质量不稳或需3-bit键。本文对KV键采用E8格向量量化，利用相邻维度相关性提升SQNR，并用查表式非对称打分避免显式码本反量化。在五个模型家族上实现约6倍KV压缩、比标量k3v2小约20%，长上下文困惑度接近基线且解码吞吐持平。该工作以低开销原语扩展质量-显存前沿。
papers.abstract_en: Compressing the key-value (KV) cache is essential for serving long-context large language models (LLMs) under memory constraints. While current scalar quantization methods achieve significant compression, they typically face a quality-fidelity trade-off, either suffering from performance instability at 2-bit precision or necessitating 3-bit keys to maintain model quality. In this work, we demonstrate that a uniform low-bit k2v2 configuration (2-bit keys and 2-bit values) can preserve near-baseline quality by using vector quantization (VQ) based on the $E_8$ lattice for KV keys. We show that structured VQ exploits correlations across adjacent dimensions to achieve signal-to-quantization-noise ratios (SQNR) higher than those of independent scalar quantization at the same key payload rate. To ensure practical utility, we adapt a table-based asymmetric scoring algorithm that avoids explicit codebook dequantization during attention computation and preserves decode-throughput parity with scalar baselines. Across five LLM families, our $E_8$ k2v2 approach yields \textasciitilde$6\times$ KV compression, roughly 20\% smaller than scalar k3v2 (3-bit keys and 2-bit values), while retaining near-baseline long-context perplexity. In our full-suite perplexity evaluation, $E_8$ improves over scalar k3v2 in 80\% of model--dataset--context settings. These results indicate that $E_8$ lattice VQ improves quality per byte while keeping throughput at parity, suggesting that structured key quantization is a useful primitive for KV-compression stacks. Overall, our work provides a low-overhead primitive for expanding the quality-memory frontier in long-context LLM inference.

papers.title_en: WUSPruner: Second-Moment-Optimal Transforms for Structured Pruning
papers.authors: Shengkun Tang, Dan Alistarh, Zhiqiang Shen
papers.evidence: 面向 LLM 结构化剪枝的变换基底选择
papers.tldr: 结构化剪枝通常直接在原坐标系删除维度，但删除误差高度依赖所选基。WUSPruner将基选择建模为局部线性重建问题，联合激活与权重二阶矩构造WUS变换，使二者同时对角化并平衡，从而分解删除误差并指导坐标选择。基于分块变换和紧凑输入投影的可扩展剪枝方法，在Llama与Qwen 8B至72B模型上稳定优于基线，并降低推理延迟与内存。该工作为面向坐标删除的基选择提供了二阶矩最优的理论依据。
papers.abstract_en: Structured pruning is typically formulated as identifying which model dimensions to remove, often within the model's original representation. However, the effect of coordinate deletion fundamentally depends on the basis in which pruning is performed. This raises a more fundamental question: how should the basis be chosen specifically for coordinate deletion? We introduce WUSPruner, a transform-based framework for structured pruning of large language models. We formulate basis selection as a local linear reconstruction problem that directly minimizes the reconstruction loss induced by pruning. Inspired by the second-moment transformation in WUSH, we consider a WUS transform constructed jointly from activation and weight statistics. We show that under positive-definite second moments, WUS transform minimizes the local reconstruction loss over all invertible changes of basis. In the resulting basis, the activation and weight second moments are simultaneously diagonalized and balanced, causing the deletion error to decompose into independent spectral contributions and yielding a principled criterion for coordinate selection. Guided by this result, we develop a scalable pruning method based on blockwise WUS transformations and compact input projections. Experiments on Llama and Qwen models from 8B to 72B parameters show consistent improvements over structured pruning baselines across language modeling, knowledge, commonsense reasoning, mathematics, and code generation benchmarks, while also delivering practical reductions in inference latency and memory usage.

papers.title_en: GA-SVD: Generation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for LLM Compression
papers.authors: Shengkun Tang, Cong Zeng, Zongfang Liu, Dan Alistarh, Zhiqiang Shen
papers.evidence: 面向 LLM 内存效率的一次性低秩压缩
papers.tldr: 大模型参数规模带来内存与计算开销，一次性低秩压缩虽具潜力，但现有SVD方法偏重选择题评测，生成任务性能下降且秩分配依赖启发式。GA-SVD提出生成感知低秩压缩框架：用在线策略知识蒸馏梯度构建生成对齐的白化变换，并以进化算法在全局压缩率下搜索逐层秩分配。在Mistral-7B、Qwen3与Llama-3.3上，该方法在选择题和生成基准均优于现有SVD基线并取得SoTA，且可扩展至70B参数模型。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong generalization across a broad range of reasoning and generation tasks, but their large parameter counts impose substantial memory and computation costs, hindering deployment in practical resource-constrained settings. One-shot low-rank compression is a promising solution since it reduces model size and inference cost effectively. However, existing SVD-based methods primarily target multiple-choice benchmarks and often fail to preserve performance on generation tasks. Moreover, their rank allocation strategies are typically heuristic. We propose GA-SVD, a generation-aware low-rank compression framework for LLMs. First, we introduce Generation-Aware Weight Whitening (GAWW), which leverages gradients from on-policy knowledge distillation to construct whitening transformations aligned with generative behavior. Second, we develop an evolutionary global rank allocation method that searches for effective layer-wise rank allocation under a given global compression ratio. Across extensive experiments on Mistral-7B, Qwen3 series, and Llama-3.3 models, evaluated on both multiple-choice and generative benchmarks, GA-SVD consistently outperforms existing SVD-based baselines and achieves state-of-the-art (SoTA) results. We further demonstrate scalability by applying our method to models with up to 70B parameters.

papers.title_en: Recovering Low-Bit Failures in Vision-Language-Action Policies via Quantization-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Seongmin Park, Jaewon Lee, Yujun Heo, Yoonsik Kim, Seheon Choi, Hyoung-rock Kim, Jungwook Choi
papers.evidence: 视觉语言动作策略在视觉与语义偏移下的量化敏感性
papers.tldr: 视觉-语言-动作策略量化能降低部署成本，但在长时程和视觉/语义偏移下会损害任务完成。作者基于5个VLA模型、4050次真机试验，提出量化条件强化学习QCRL，以进度优势估计和量化感知源条件利用FP rollout的结果信号。在π0.5的INT4 W4A16上达到FP均分的99.3%并省42.9%模型显存；NVFP4 W4A4上达100.7%且部署加速1.73倍。该工作为低比特VLA策略提供了结果驱动的恢复方案。
papers.abstract_en: Quantization lowers deployment costs of vision-language-action (VLA) policies but can compromise task completion. Across five VLA models and 4,050 real-world trials, we systematically reveal that quantization-aware training (QAT) generally improves on post-training quantization (PTQ) but leaves substantial gaps to full precision (FP) on long-horizon tasks and under visual and semantic shifts, while its imitation-based objective does not explicitly use rollout success or partial completion. To exploit these outcome signals, we introduce Quantization-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning (QCRL), an offline RL method coupling progress-based advantage estimation with quantization-aware source conditioning. FP rollouts supply reference experience beyond action-level distillation, progress-scaled terminal penalty distinguishes partial completion, and quantization-aware conditioning selects advantageous reference behavior within the quantized policy. We evaluate weight-only INT4 W4A16 on $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.5 and joint weight-activation NVFP4 W4A4 on $π_{0.5}$. Using only in-distribution data, QCRL reaches 99.3% of FP's mean score across three visual-shift conditions for $π_{0.5}$ with INT4 W4A16, alongside 42.9% model-memory savings. With NVFP4 W4A4, it reaches 100.7% of the same FP baseline, alongside a $1.73\times$ speedup using NVFP4/FP8 deployment. Hardware gains are relative to FP16 on Jetson Thor.

papers.title_en: Preserving Updates in Low-Bit Recurrent State Quantization
papers.authors: Haotian Li, Liran Dong, Kaicheng Xiao, Guoliang Xing
papers.evidence: 低秩旁路保留低比特量化舍入中丢失的小更新
papers.tldr: 循环状态每步更新后需重新量化，低比特误差会跨步累积且高度相干，仅降低单步误差不够。作者提出免训练的低秩旁路LRB，用小缓冲累积微小更新并周期性合并；同时提出有界方向舍入BDR，在舍入时避免状态元素反向。在Gated DeltaNet、GLA、Mamba2和RetNet上，该方法显著优于INT4，状态内存最多降5.3倍，解码最多加速1.9倍。
papers.abstract_en: Linear attention and recurrent models compress past tokens into a fixed-size state that is updated at every step. However, storing these states in high precision incurs substantial memory and bandwidth costs at large batch sizes, motivating low-bit state quantization. Unlike weights and key--value caches, a recurrent state is requantized after every update, so its quantization errors accumulate across steps. Our analysis shows that these errors are highly coherent across steps, so reducing per-step errors alone is insufficient. This coherence arises mainly from small updates that are lost in rounding. To preserve these updates, we intervene both before and at rounding. Before rounding, we propose Low-Rank Bypass (LRB), which accumulates small updates in a compact low-rank buffer and periodically merges its sufficiently large elements into the state. At rounding, we observe that a state element can even move opposite to its update, and such reversals prove particularly harmful. Therefore, we propose Bounded Directional Rounding (BDR), which rounds reversed elements toward their updates without additional storage. Although BDR enlarges the rounding error, it improves the model, suggesting that the direction of an update matters more than its rounding error at a single step. Across Gated DeltaNet, GLA, Mamba2, and RetNet, our training-free method substantially outperforms INT4, while reducing state memory by up to 5.3$\times$ and speeding up decoding by up to 1.9$\times$ relative to FP32 states.
